display.title: Tanya Shiur 56: Chapter 23, Mitzvos as the King's Limbs, and Ahavas Yisroel
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Tanya shiur on chapter 23: Torah and Hashem are one, mitzvos are like the limbs of the King, followed by a talk on loving every Jew.
display.summary_long: Shiur 56 in Rabbi Yosef Goldstein's Yiddish Tanya series. It opens with an introduction: Torah is light, and Chassidus, the inner part of the Torah, teaches us to see the inner side of everything rather than its outer shell. The difference between 'chefetz' (inner desire) and 'ratzon' (outer will) is explained with the example of a man who works only for the sake of the satisfaction it brings; Hashem's inner desire is a dwelling place in this lowest world, and the word 'barasi' hints at the 613 mitzvos. The class then studies Tanya chapter 23: the Zohar calls Torah and Hashem 'entirely one', while the Tikkunim call the mitzvos 'the limbs of the King'. Just as a hand moves the instant a person wills it, the mitzvah act becomes wholly given over to Hashem's will and draws His light into all the worlds. The last part is a talk on Ahavas Yisroel, tied to the Rebbe's new booklet on the subject: the Baal Shem Tov's teaching to love every single Jew, the Alter Rebbe's parable of a tarnished gold cup, the Rambam's laws of loving one's fellow and the convert, and why the Alter Rebbe's siddur places 'I hereby accept the mitzvah of loving my fellow' before davening, as the Frierdiker Rebbe learned at his bar mitzvah.
display.lesson: Every mitzvah joins a Jew to Hashem's innermost will, and nothing gives Hashem more pleasure than seeing one Jew love another; accepting Ahavas Yisroel before davening opens the gates for our prayers.

date.note: The next shiur (57) says '5737' on air and is just before Purim; this one is a week earlier and recalls the recent talk on machatzis hashekel.
